nodes.name: Low-temperature CoS_x film deposition
nodes.procedure: Cu@CoS_x/CF is synthesized by directly depositing CoS_x film on CF in ethanol at 70°C by using the chemical reaction between thioacetamide, a source of sulfur, and Co²⁺ ions. During the deposition of CoS_x film, the CF serves as the source of Cu atoms that self-diffuse into the as-formed CoS_x film, besides serving as a support material. This process ultimately results in the formation of novel Cu@CoS_x/CF nanocomposite materials (Figure 1A and see the Experimental Section for details).

nodes.description: OER and HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 3A, Cu@CoS_x/CF exhibits a remarkable catalytic activity for both OER and HER. Cu@CoS_x/CF affords current densities of 10 and 100mAcm^{-2} at ≈160 and 310mV for OER... In the case of HER, Cu@CoS_x/CF also exhibits an excellent electrocatalytic activity, with current densities of 10 and 100mAcm^{-2} at 134 and 267mV

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (OWS) in two-electrode alkaline electrolyzer
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 3C, the electrolyzer assembled by Cu@CoS_x/CF-Cu@CoS_x/CF couple affords current densities of 10 and 100mAcm^{-2} at ≈1.50 and 1.80V at 25°C... the energy efficiency of the Cu@CoS_x/CF -based electrolyzer is found to be as high as 98.7% at 10mA cm^{-2} and 82.2% at 100mA cm^{-2}... after 200h of the water splitting reaction at 1.8V, the Cu@CoS_x/CF -based electrolyzer maintains the current output of 100mA cm^{-2} without any degradation

the potentiostatic OER and HER in the presence of Cu@CoS_x/CF are carried out for more than 20h at a high current density of >100mA cm^{-2}. As revealed in Figure S5, there is no noticeable current density degradation for both OER and HER... The results show that the Cu@CoS_x/CF gives nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency for both OER and HER
As shown in Figure 4B, the ECSA of CoS_x/CF is about 5.2 times larger than that of Co_9S_8/CF

By fitting the experimental data to equivalent circuit model... the series resistance (R_s), and charge-transfer resistances (R_ct) for the materials are extracted... Cu@CoS_x/CF has smaller R_s and R_ct values than CoS_x/CF and Co_9S_8/CF

nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure 1D) reveal that the entire CF surface is fully covered by a rough Cu@CoS_x film with a thickness of ≈500 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: No lattice fringes are observed in the HRTEM image, demonstrating the amorphous nature of the Cu@CoS_x film. SAED pattern exhibits a typical halo for amorphous materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, no lattice fringes are observed in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Figure 1E), demonstrating the amorphous nature of the Cu@CoS_x film. This is further confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED), which exhibits a typical halo around the bright spot in the center for amorphous materials (Figure 1E, inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping reveals that the Cu, Co, and S elements are homogeneously distributed over the Cu@CoS_x film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further elemental mapping analysis (Figure 1F) reveals that the Cu, Co, and S elements are homogeneously distributed over the Cu@CoS_x film.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy reveals that Cu@CoS_x/CF has a loading of ≈3.9 mg Cu@CoS_x/cm² CF and a molar ratio of Cu: Co: S is about 1.15: 1.28: 1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu@CoS_x film supported on CF is dominated by amorphous materials, only with a small amount of very tiny Co₉S₈ crystallites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Taken together, the two XRD results show that the Cu@CoS_x film supported on CF is dominated by the amorphous materials, only with a small amount of very tiny Co₉S₈ crystallites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu@CoS_x/CF exhibits a similar Raman spectrum to the previously reported Co₉S₈ crystalline materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This speculation is in line with the Raman result (Figure S2, Supporting Information), which shows that Cu@CoS_x/CF exhibits a similar Raman spectrum to the previously reported Co₉S₈ crystalline materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows 1s→3d pre-edge peak at 7709.7 eV consistent with Co(II), edge position at 7715.1 eV indicating average oxidation state between 0 and +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES spectrum of Cu@CoS_x shows a 1s→3d pre-edge peak at 7709.7 eV, which is consistent with a character of Co(II). Additionally, the edge position (7715.1 eV) for Cu@CoS_x lies between the edges for CoO (7717.1 eV) and for Co foil (7710.8 eV), indicating that an average oxidation of cobalt intermediates between 0 and +2.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT of K³-weighted Co EXAFS resolves Co-S distances at 2.20 Å and Co-Co distances at 2.50 Å with lower coordination numbers than crystalline Co₉S₈.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the first shell of the FT clearly resolves Co-S distances at 2.20 Å and Co-Co distances at 2.50 Å (see the fitting structural parameters in Table S1, Supporting Information), which are in agreement with those obtained from Co₉S₈ crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES lacks pre-edge peak of Cu(II) and characteristic edge-rising peak of Cu(I), absorption edge identical to Cu foil but with attenuated post-edge oscillations indicating small Cu clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The comparison result reveals that the Cu K-edge XANES of Cu@CoS_x contains neither the pre-edge peak arising from Cu(II) 1s→3d transition nor the characteristic edge-rising peak at ≈8981.1 eV originating from Cu(I) 1s→4p transition. In contrast, the absorption edge energy and shape for Cu@CoS_x are almost identical to those of Cu foil, but the post-edge oscillations obviously attenuate for Cu@CoS_x, compared with Cu foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT of Cu K-edge EXAFS shows coordination number of 3.4 for copper in Cu@CoS_x, much lower than 12 for bulk copper, indicating sub-nanometric metal clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To more specific, copper has a coordination number of 3.4 for Cu@CoS_x, which is much lower than that (a coordination number of 12) for bulk copper (Table S2, Supporting Information).
